title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: Noli — peccatum ≠ poena proprie
pass_a_gloss: Do not object to me that sin is sometimes the punishment of sin. For first it is not punishment insofar as it is sin, unless you wish to confuse two opposite species of evil with each other, the distinction between the evil of punishment and of fault having been removed. But privation of justice in us, as such, is formally sin; for it is repugnant to the law. Next that is not to be taken of punishment properly and strictly accepted, such as the law threatens and justice necessarily demands that satisfaction be made to itself. For who would believe that justice demands that justice be violated? that justice be satisfied by that by which justice is injured? that the debt of punishment be paid by that by which that debt is increased? that there be joined to the precept, lest it be violated, a threat of punishment situated in the violation of the precept? I proceed therefore.
pass_b_english: Do not tell me that sin is sometimes the punishment of sin. First, sin as sin is not punishment—unless you mean to smash together two opposite kinds of evil and erase the line between penalty and guilt. Privation of righteousness in us, as such, is formally sin; it clashes with the law.

Second, that claim is not about punishment properly and strictly so called—the kind the law threatens and justice must have satisfied. Who believes justice demands that justice be broken? that justice is paid by wounding justice? that the penalty-debt is settled by making the debt larger? that a threat whose penalty is the very breach of the precept should be tacked onto the precept "do not break it"? I go on.
source_text: Noli mihi objicere peccatum esse interdum poenam peccati. Primum enim non est poena quatenus peccatum, nisi velis duas species mali oppositas inter se confundere, sublato inter malum poenae & culpae discrimine. Privatio autem justitiae in nobis, qua talis, formaliter peccatum est; repugnat enim legi. Deinde id non est accipiendum de poena proprie & stricte accepta, qualem lex comminatur & justitia necessario exigit ut sibi satisfiat. Quis enim credat justitiam exigere ut justitia violetur? satisfieri justitiae eo quo justitia laeditur? solvi poenae debitum eo, quo debitum illud augetur? Adjungi praecepto, ne violetur, comminationem poenae sitae in violatione praecepti? pergo igitur.
